items.followUp: Define pressure and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Checks the defining relationship for density.
rubric.description: Defines density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that density is mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: Checks the correct SI unit for density.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of density.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving kg m⁻³ or an equivalent form such as kg/m³.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
The SI unit of density is kg m⁻³.

items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the third equation of motion, v² = vᵢ² + 2as.

rubric.why: Checks that the graph has the correct axes and represents uniform acceleration.
rubric.description: Draws and labels the velocity-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for time on the horizontal axis, velocity on the vertical axis, and a straight line from initial velocity vi to final velocity vf.

rubric.why: Checks that displacement is identified as the area under the graph and expressed as the rectangle plus triangle.
rubric.description: Expresses displacement as the areas under the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for S = vit + ½(vf − vi)t, or an equivalent area decomposition.

rubric.why: Checks use of the acceleration relationship to replace the change in velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a = (vf − vi)/t or vf − vi = at.

rubric.why: Checks that the required equation follows from the area expression and acceleration relationship.
rubric.description: Obtains the second equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final result S = vit + ½at².

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time t (s) on the horizontal axis and velocity v (m s⁻¹) on the vertical axis.
Plot the points (0, vi) and (t, vf), where vf = vi + at, and join them with a straight line.
Displacement S is the area under the velocity-time graph.
S = area of rectangle + area of triangle = vit + ½(vf − vi)t.
Since a = (vf − vi)/t, then vf − vi = at.
Therefore, S = vit + ½at².

items.followUp: Explain how to locate the centre of gravity of a flat, regular shape.

rubric.why: Checks the standard definition of centre of gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the point through which the whole weight of a body appears to act.

rubric.why: Checks the first step of the practical method.
rubric.description: Suspends the irregular shape from a point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for suspending the irregular shape freely from a pin or support.

rubric.why: Checks how the vertical through the suspension point is recorded.
rubric.description: Marks the vertical line using a plumb line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for hanging a plumb line from the suspension point and marking its line on the shape.

rubric.why: Checks that the procedure is repeated and the intersection locates the centre of gravity.
rubric.description: Repeats the procedure and locates the intersection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for suspending from another point, marking the new vertical line, and identifying the intersection of the lines as the centre of gravity.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body appears to act.
Make a small hole near the edge of the irregular shape and suspend it freely from a pin through the hole.
Hang a plumb line from the same pin and mark the vertical line on the shape.
Suspend the shape from a second point and mark the new vertical line using the plumb line.
The intersection of the two marked lines is the centre of gravity.

items.followUp: How many significant figures are in 0.00630 m? Give one other example of a measurement and its number of significant figures.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of significant figures in a measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that significant figures include all certain digits and the first uncertain or estimated digit.

rubric.why: Checks that two measurement examples and their significant-figure counts are supplied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving two valid measurement examples and identifying the significant figures in each.

modelAnswer: The significant figures of a measurement are all its certain digits together with its first uncertain (estimated) digit.
Examples: 2.35 cm has 3 significant figures; 0.0042 kg has 2 significant figures.

items.followUp: A screw gauge reads +0.03 mm when its jaws are closed. State the type of zero error and how it is recognized.

rubric.why: Checks the sign and identifying position for positive zero error.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that, with the jaws closed, the circular-scale zero lies below the reference line, giving a positive reading.

rubric.why: Checks the sign and identifying position for negative zero error.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that, with the jaws closed, the circular-scale zero lies above the reference line, giving a negative reading.

modelAnswer: When the screw-gauge jaws are closed, a positive zero error occurs if the zero of the circular scale lies below the reference line.
A negative zero error occurs if the zero of the circular scale lies above the reference line.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a base quantity and a derived quantity, and state how a derived quantity is obtained.

rubric.why: Checks the defining distinction for base quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that base quantities are independent and are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.

rubric.why: Checks the defining relationship for derived quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that derived quantities are obtained by mathematical combination of base quantities.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent physical quantities that are not defined in terms of other quantities.
Derived quantities are obtained by mathematical combination of base quantities.

items.followUp: On a distance-time graph, identify the independent and dependent variables and their axes.

rubric.why: Checks the role and usual graph position of the independent variable.
rubric.description: Defines and locates the independent variable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the independent variable is chosen or controlled and is plotted on the horizontal (x) axis.

rubric.why: Checks the role and usual graph position of the dependent variable.
rubric.description: Defines and locates the dependent variable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the dependent variable changes in response to the independent variable and is plotted on the vertical (y) axis.

modelAnswer: The independent variable is the quantity chosen or controlled; it is plotted on the horizontal (x) axis.
The dependent variable is the quantity that changes in response to the independent variable; it is plotted on the vertical (y) axis.
